core_obligations: Translate the algebraic condition to the fibre: for a pair consisting of a prime of the chart and the corresponding point, let s be the image point and let the prime under the given prime be the one corresponding to s; then the given prime is a relative associated prime of the module exactly when the prime of the base changed module corresponding to the point is associated, by the cited comparison (proof lines 1100-1107).

Identify the base changed module geometrically: the residue field tensor product corresponds to the fibre of the affine chart over s and the base changed module corresponds to the restriction of the fibrewise sheaf, so the point is an associated point of the restriction of the sheaf to its fibre, which is the relative associated point condition of the statement (proof lines 1108-1112).

Reverse implication: the converse direction follows when the prime of the fibre is finitely generated, which is the hypothesis in the last sentence of the statement, namely that all fibres are locally Noetherian (proof lines 1113-1117).
proof_roadmap: Pass from relative associated primes of the module to associated primes of its base change to the residue field of the image point (proof lines 1100-1107).
Read that condition geometrically through the affine description of associated points on the fibre, and note that finite generation of the fibre prime gives the converse (proof lines 1108-1117).
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates the relative associated primes of the module of sections over a pair of affine charts to the relative associated points of the sheaf, with the converse requiring finitely generated fibre primes, which is the case when all fibres are locally Noetherian (statement lines 1078-1095). The counted proof is short and complete: it converts the algebraic condition into an associatedness condition on the base change of the module to the residue field of the image point, identifies that base change with the restriction of the fibrewise sheaf, and applies the affine description of associated points on the fibre; the converse is reduced to the finite generation of the fibre prime (proof lines 1097-1117). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard relative associated prime comparison and the affine description of associated points.
